title: Repository Source Documentation And Linting Adoption Delivery
summary: Promote the Docs Viewer pilot into repository-owned source-documentation and lint tooling with maintained application boundaries and staged adoption.
content_html:
Repository Source Documentation And Linting Adoption Delivery

Complete Result

JavaScript and Python applications across the repository can use one reproducible source-documentation and lint capability without treating Docs Viewer as their tooling owner.

The completed result provides:

  • repository-owned Ruff and ESLint pins, configuration, installation, and direct commands;
  • maintained application source boundaries with explicit runtime contexts and exclusions;
  • useful JSDoc and Python docstrings on new, materially changed, and high-value existing contracts;
  • clean adopted boundaries for Studio, Admin, Docs Viewer, public-site, shared-frontend, and site-tools source;
  • normal check-profile coverage that reports its exact maintained targets;
  • path-filtered CI enforcement only after the relevant maintained boundary is clean.

This delivery was approved for implementation on 2026-07-26.

Why This Delivery Exists

The Docs Viewer pilot proved practical conventions and low-noise Ruff and ESLint rules on four representative files. It deliberately located tooling under docs-viewer/, force-excluded other applications, required delivery-specific explicit paths, and did not join a normal check profile.

Those decisions were correct for the pilot but now prevent Studio and other applications from adopting the capability without duplicating or misrepresenting ownership. Repository adoption must replace that pilot boundary rather than merely remove exclusions from Docs Viewer configuration.

Benefits And Risks

Benefits

  • New and unfamiliar code gains concise contract information at its source.
  • Cheap correctness and unused-code defects are caught before broader tests or manual review.
  • Studio and other applications can adopt one pinned toolchain while retaining their actual runtime and ownership boundaries.
  • Maintained scope checks replace fixed specimens and false application-wide confidence.
  • Local, cloud, check-profile, and CI command shapes become reproducible.

Risks

  • A broad first run can turn historical debt into noisy unrelated churn.
  • Generic browser or Python assumptions can hide real application contexts.
  • Existing path-bootstrap imports and suppressions can be excused too broadly instead of reviewed.
  • Automatic fixes can conceal behavioural changes or delete intentionally side-effectful imports.
  • Premature CI enforcement can block unrelated work before an application boundary is clean.

Mitigate these risks through named maintained targets, audit-first cleanup, bounded source-area adoption, local justified suppressions, and profile or CI promotion only after a whole maintained boundary passes.

Decisions

Repository Tool Owner

Create one repository development-tool owner under tooling/lint/. It owns:

  • the Ruff development dependency pin and shared Python baseline;
  • the private ESLint package, direct dependency pins, and lockfile;
  • labelled ESLint configuration blocks for each real JavaScript context;
  • maintained target definitions for application and shared source;
  • ignored local environments, dependency trees, and caches.

This is a repository development-tool package, not a runtime JavaScript application or a replacement for feature-local packages. The isolated Mermaid renderer keeps its own package and lifecycle.

Commands

Provide repository-root commands with two truthful modes:

  • bin/lint-python <path> [path ...] and bin/lint-js <path> [path ...] lint exact submitted new or changed paths;
  • bin/lint --scope <scope-id> lints the complete maintained boundary for one adopted scope.

All commands fail on missing or empty targets and report the resolved paths. The scope command resolves checked configuration rather than embedding a historical fixed-file list.

Cut over current documentation and callers and remove the Docs Viewer lint wrappers in the same change. Do not retain compatibility aliases.

Shared Baseline And Application Context

The repository owns the initial low-noise rules:

  • Ruff E4, E7, E9, and F;
  • ESLint recommended correctness rules;
  • no automatic fixes;
  • unused ESLint disable directives are errors.

Applications own:

  • maintained source roots;
  • browser ESM, Node, worker, or test globals and module settings;
  • path-specific exclusions;
  • justified local or per-path exceptions;
  • the point at which a whole boundary joins normal checks.

Do not use one generic JavaScript globals set across unrelated code. Do not enable broader Ruff categories, formatting, complexity limits, TypeScript, or missing-documentation enforcement in this delivery.

Source Documentation

Retain the proven authoring rules:

  • types describe types; comments explain meaning;
  • document exported or public APIs when callers need lifecycle, ownership, ordering, side effects, failure, invariant, unit, or constrained-value information;
  • use JavaScript typedefs for stable shared object and callback shapes;
  • let Python annotations carry types and use docstrings for domain behaviour;
  • do not document trivial helpers or restate signatures;
  • simplify or split confused ownership rather than explain it with a long comment;
  • update a source comment in the same change as its contract.

This delivery does not select or publish generated API/reference pages. JSDoc and docstrings must be useful in source and editor help without a generator.

Maintained Target Model

The exact paths are confirmed in RSDL-P0. The initial model is:

Scope Python source JavaScript source
studio Studio server, services, shared Python, commands, and checks Studio frontend modules and route modules
admin Admin server, checks, commands, and reports Admin frontend modules and route modules
docs-viewer Docs Viewer services and Python builders Manage-owned and site-owned Docs Viewer browser modules
public-site Site validation tooling where not owned by site-tools Public catalogue, search, shell, and theme modules
shared Any later repository-shared Python boundary Shared frontend modules
site-tools Site validation package and commands None currently

Tests use separate target contexts. Generated data, published payloads, vendor source, dependency trees, caches, retired source, recovery archives, and canonical data remain excluded.

The Admin target map is useful ownership evidence but is not itself lint configuration: it includes non-code families and overlapping public/shared surfaces. RSDL-P0 should reconcile the two configurations and add a focused drift check rather than make one silently derive unsupported runtime settings from the other.

Starting Evidence

A read-only audit using the pilot's low-noise Python rules and a common browser ESM ESLint baseline produced the following indicative findings:

Maintained area Python JavaScript
Studio 59 104
Admin 15 12
Docs Viewer active services/build/runtime 73 31
Public-site JavaScript — 22
Shared frontend — 0
Site tools 0 —

These are planning evidence, not accepted baselines. Tests were excluded and the JavaScript audit did not yet model every final application context.

Studio's Python findings included undefined names, unused imports and variables, import placement, and loop-variable shadowing. Its JavaScript findings were mainly unused variables and useless assignments, with smaller numbers of caught-error preservation, empty-block, escape, and undefined-name findings.

Every finding must be classified as:

  • genuine defect;
  • safe mechanical cleanup;
  • design or ownership review;
  • justified local exception;
  • configuration or runtime-context error.

Do not use a checked blanket baseline file to hide known findings. Adopt clean directories progressively if a whole application cannot be cleaned in one reviewable batch.

Implemented Baseline

RSDL-P0 replaced the indicative scan with checked application contexts. The accepted audit before cleanup was:

Maintained scope Files Python findings JavaScript findings
shared 5 — 0
site-tools 4 0 —
studio 184 30 48
admin 41 5 3
public-site 25 — 3
docs-viewer 240 122 15
tests 209 43 —

The accepted maintained total is 708 files: 436 Python and 272 JavaScript. The checked target map is tooling/lint/targets.json. A focused contract test keeps application roots visible to the broader Admin target map without deriving lint globals or source roles from it. Shared frontend and the multi-owner test context remain explicit lint-only boundaries.

Findings resolved as:

  • genuine defects: missing Catalogue lookup-refresh imports, an undefined Studio Tag Registry status call, and stale direct-script test invocations;
  • safe cleanup: unused imports, values, assignments, and unreachable local wrappers;
  • reviewed exceptions: exact path-bootstrap entrypoints and active façade re-exports only;
  • configuration: separate browser ESM blocks and explicit generated, vendor, canonical, retired, dependency, cache, and Processing exclusions.

No baseline file, automatic fix, formatter, TypeScript, or compatibility alias was introduced.

Shipped Capability

  • tooling/lint/ owns Ruff 0.16.0, ESLint 10.8.0, @eslint/js 10.0.1, globals 17.7.0, both configurations, the lockfile, and maintained targets.
  • bin/lint-python and bin/lint-js require eligible explicit paths. bin/lint --scope <scope-id> resolves a complete checked boundary and reports its language, file count, and roots.
  • .codex/setup.sh and the dev container install the isolated lint environments; the Mermaid renderer remains independent.
  • source-lint is the intentional aggregate profile and is a child of full. App-owned profiles include their relevant maintained scope without duplicating execution in combined runs.
  • .github/workflows/source-lint.yml installs from the checked pins and runs all adopted scopes when their source, configuration, setup, or lint tooling changes.
  • New runner and profile contracts prove missing, empty, excluded, unknown, Python-defect, JavaScript-defect, scope-drift, coverage-summary, and aggregate-deduplication failures.
  • The new runner contracts carry source docstrings for path rejection, repository-local tool ownership, and evidence reporting. Other cleanup did not change exported contracts and did not justify documentation churn.

Backfill Order

Backfill source documentation by value and risk:

  1. shared and cross-application contracts;
  2. exported JavaScript options, callbacks, events, controllers, and lifecycle boundaries;
  3. Python services, adapters, value objects, write plans, builders, commands, and error translation;
  4. stateful or side-effectful modules that repeatedly require source archaeology;
  5. complex code where documenting the contract exposes a useful simplification.

Do not backfill trivial accessors, obvious wrappers, generated/vendor source, or test functions whose names and fixtures already state the contract.

Delivery Checkpoints

[x] RSDL-P0 — Freeze Maintained Boundaries And Audit

  • Inventory tracked Python and JavaScript source by application, owner, runtime context, and source/test/generated/vendor/retired role.
  • Confirm supported Python, Node, and npm environments from current repository setup.
  • Define checked maintained-target configuration and its relationship to the Admin target map.
  • Re-run audit-only Ruff and ESLint commands for every proposed target.
  • Record categorized findings and split cleanup into reviewable source areas.
  • Confirm generated, vendor, canonical-data, recovered, retired, dependency, and cache exclusions.

Checkpoint: accepted configuration and baseline evidence define what repository-wide adoption means without changing source or enforcing lint.

[x] RSDL-P1 — Establish Repository Tooling

  • Create the repository-owned Python and JavaScript lint dependency owners, exact pins, lockfile, shared configurations, and target definitions.
  • Add generic explicit-path and maintained-scope commands with missing-target failure.
  • Move ignored local lint environments and caches to repository-tooling locations.
  • Update local/cloud/container setup so the supported environment can install and run both toolchains reproducibly.
  • Preserve the Mermaid renderer's independent package.
  • Cut stable guidance and direct callers to the repository commands, then remove the Docs Viewer wrappers and tracked pilot tooling without aliases.
  • Add focused command/configuration tests that catch ignored-target and false-green regressions.

Checkpoint: a clean checkout can install the tools and lint explicit paths for any configured application without Docs Viewer ownership.

[x] RSDL-P2 — Adopt Shared Source, Site Tools, And Studio

  • Promote the already-clean shared frontend and site-tools boundaries first.
  • Clean Studio Python in bounded server, shared, service, command, and check areas.
  • Clean Studio JavaScript in bounded shared, Catalogue, Tag, and route areas.
  • Review every E402, noqa, type-ignore, ESLint disable, and intentional side-effect import reached by the selected rules.
  • Add useful JSDoc and docstrings to new, materially changed, and Priority 1 Studio contracts encountered during cleanup.
  • Require the full maintained Studio Python and JavaScript scopes to pass.
  • Run focused Studio contract evidence separately from lint.

Checkpoint: Studio can use exact-path lint during delivery work and has clean full-scope commands suitable for normal check integration.

[x] RSDL-P3 — Adopt Admin, Public Site, Docs Viewer, And Tests

  • Clean and promote the maintained Admin Python and JavaScript boundaries.
  • Clean and promote public-site JavaScript without changing the tracked static deployment model.
  • Expand Docs Viewer from the four pilot specimens to its complete maintained Python and JavaScript boundaries.
  • Add separate Python test and JavaScript test/tool contexts where they provide maintainable correctness feedback.
  • Review cross-application imports and shared modules under their real owner rather than linting duplicate projections.
  • Backfill only the high-value contracts reached by each bounded cleanup.

Checkpoint: every active repository Python/JavaScript application and shared source area has a passing maintained boundary or an explicitly separate project lifecycle.

[x] RSDL-P4 — Integrate Normal Checks And CI

  • Add app-owned maintained lint commands to the smallest useful run_checks.py profiles.
  • Add an intentional aggregate source-lint profile and decide explicitly whether it belongs in full.
  • Report the resolved maintained targets and rule/config owner in run summaries.
  • Add path-filtered CI installation and lint jobs only for clean adopted boundaries.
  • Keep exact-path delivery commands available; a green aggregate must not obscure omitted or separately owned source.
  • Prove failures for a genuine Python defect, JavaScript defect, excluded generated/vendor path, empty target, and unsupported scope.

Checkpoint: local checks and CI prevent regression across every adopted boundary without blocking separately owned projects.

[x] RSDL-P5 — Stable Guidance And Closeout

  • Update the Development Checklist with generic commands and maintained-scope rules.
  • Update Run Checks, Runtime Dependencies, cloud/container setup, and source ownership documentation with the shipped extension method.
  • Retain the completed Docs Viewer pilot as historical proving evidence while making repository tooling the current authority.
  • Record remaining rule-expansion, formatter, type-checking, reference generation, and project-specific adoption opportunities separately.
  • Run the mandatory end-of-delivery review and reconcile every coverage claim with exact maintained targets and evidence.
  • Present the feature, concept, pilot, this delivery, and durable owners for closeout review.

Checkpoint: current durable guidance routes directly to repository-owned tooling and application-owned maintained boundaries.

Processing Boundary

processing/ remains a separate Java/Processing project. Its recovered sketches, bundled library examples, templates, and active projects cannot be treated as one maintained application source root.

This delivery records but does not invent its future lifecycle:

  • identify active first-party Processing source separately from recovered, example, library, and template material;
  • use Javadoc rather than JSDoc for Java-mode public contracts;
  • select Processing-aware Java formatting, linting, build, and test commands only when that project lifecycle is defined.

Repository-wide Python/JavaScript adoption must not claim Processing coverage.

Out Of Scope

  • Java/Processing tool selection or source cleanup
  • generated API/reference pages
  • repository-wide TypeScript, checkJs, or jsconfig.json
  • Python or JavaScript formatting
  • broad automatic fixes
  • complexity, nesting, parameter-count, or missing-documentation enforcement
  • runtime bundling or transpilation
  • changes to the Mermaid renderer package
  • comments on every public symbol or historical source file
  • behavioural refactors that are not required to resolve a reviewed finding

Completion Gates

  • Tool pins, lockfiles, configuration, setup, and commands are repository-owned and reproducible from a clean supported environment.
  • No application depends on Docs Viewer paths to run source linting.
  • Explicit-path commands fail on empty or fully ignored targets.
  • Maintained scope commands resolve checked, reviewable source boundaries.
  • Studio, Admin, Docs Viewer, public-site, shared-frontend, and site-tools maintained boundaries pass their selected low-noise rules.
  • Runtime globals and module settings match each JavaScript context.
  • Generated, vendor, canonical-data, retired, recovery, dependency, and cache paths cannot create false coverage.
  • New and materially changed high-value contracts follow the proven JSDoc and docstring conventions.
  • Existing suppressions reached by enabled rules have been reviewed and are fixed or locally justified.
  • Normal profile and CI claims name their actual maintained surfaces.
  • Processing remains explicitly outside the Python/JavaScript coverage claim.
  • Stable documentation reflects the shipped commands, ownership, extension method, and remaining gaps.
  • No compatibility aliases, generated reference site, formatting churn, TypeScript adoption, or unrelated behavioural cleanup entered the delivery.

Status

Complete. RSDL-P0 through RSDL-P5 moved the pilot toolchain to repository ownership, adopted seven maintained Python/JavaScript boundaries, integrated profiles and path-filtered CI, and updated the Development Checklist, Run Checks, Runtime Dependencies, Local Setup Toolchain, Source Tree Ownership, repository guidance, and generated Studio docs payloads.

Closeout evidence:

  • source-lint: seven scopes and 708 files passed;
  • command/profile contracts: 15 tests passed;
  • combined quick, admin-checks, and catalogue: 15 commands passed;
  • Docs profile: 403 tests passed, 1 skipped; source lint, Studio docs build, and search build passed;
  • Admin smoke profile: four commands passed;
  • five Studio/public module smokes and four Docs Viewer module smokes passed;
  • final Studio docs build reported 215 documents, zero warnings, and no pending writes; git diff --check passed.

The first sandboxed Docs build could not launch the Mermaid browser renderer; the same profile passed with the required browser permission. That was an environment failure, not product evidence.

The mandatory review found no remaining Python/JavaScript adoption gap inside the seven checked boundaries. It did narrow broad bootstrap exceptions to exact entrypoints and restore the intentional Admin error façade after focused tests caught its accidental removal. Formatting, wider rule sets, type checking, generated reference pages, historical source-documentation backfill, and Processing lifecycle/tool selection remain separate outcomes.
